narrativeReportMd:
# SubstanceAmount R4 to R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`SubstanceAmount` is present in R4 as a draft complex datatype derived from `BackboneElement`, but no R6 StructureDefinition or canonical reference exists. This is a hard breaking identity/removal change for validators, generated models, profiles, and R4 data using the datatype.

## Scope
This report compares the R4 `StructureDefinition/SubstanceAmount` with the R6 core package and treats inherited `Element` and `BackboneElement` behavior as out of scope. Parent artifact migrations, especially `SubstancePolymer` and `SubstanceDefinition`, are noted only as dependencies.

## Main migration themes
The main issue is not a narrow cardinality or binding change: the datatype disappeared. Migration must choose context-specific R6 elements such as `SubstanceDefinition.moiety.amount[x]`, `moiety.measurementType`, `relationship.amount[x]`, `relationship.ratioHighLimitAmount`, and `relationship.comparator`; that mapping is not lossless for every R4 `SubstanceAmount` shape.

## Highest-impact findings
1. `SubstanceAmount` has no R6 counterpart. 2. Closest R6 amount structures split and reshape the R4 content model.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed to confirm the intended R6 migration path because the local packages do not include an official cross-version ConceptMap or narrative migration note.

## Backward-compatible design observations
A deprecated compatibility datatype or explicit conversion extension could have reduced disruption, but the ballot package instead exposes only context-specific R6 substance amount fields.

## Follow-up analysis
Analyze `SubstanceDefinition`, removed R4 specialized substance resources such as `SubstancePolymer`, and the `substance-amount-type` terminology separately.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `SubstanceAmount` was removed from the R6 core package with no same-canonical datatype replacement. The top migration concerns are broken canonical/type references, loss of the reusable R4 content model, and non-lossless mapping to context-specific R6 substance amount fields. The main uncertainty is the intended official migration path, because no local official diff or ConceptMap was available.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Treat `SubstanceAmount` as a removed draft datatype. Implementers need to inventory R4 profiles, extensions, validators, and generated classes that reference `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/SubstanceAmount`, then map each use in context rather than applying a single datatype rename. R4 `amount[x]` values using `Range`, separate `amountText`, and `referenceRange.lowLimit/highLimit` need special review because the closest R6 elements do not preserve that shape directly.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high that the datatype is absent from R6 because both the expected R6 StructureDefinition path and the R6 package index lack it, and a package-wide search found no `SubstanceAmount` references. Confidence in the precise migration target is medium because the local inputs include no official diff, narrative migration page, or ConceptMap.

findings.title: SubstanceAmount datatype is absent from the R6 core package

oldState.summary: R4 defines `SubstanceAmount` as a draft non-abstract complex datatype derived from `BackboneElement`.

semanticText.short: Chemical substances are a single substance type whose primary defining element is the molecular structure.
semanticText.definition: Chemical substances are a single substance type whose primary defining element is the molecular structure; the presence of salts and solvates is captured, while purity, grade, physical form, and particle size are not part of the defining substance ID.

oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, `SubstanceAmount` is a named reusable datatype with canonical URL `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/SubstanceAmount`. Generated models and profiles can refer to it as a concrete complex type.

newState.summary: No R6 `SubstanceAmount` StructureDefinition or canonical reference was found.
newState.narrativeMd: The R6 package contains `Substance` and `SubstanceDefinition` resources, plus R6 amount-related elements inside `SubstanceDefinition`, but no datatype named `SubstanceAmount` and no package reference to that name.

facts.note: No same-canonical R6 StructureDefinition was found in `.index.json`.

facts.oldValue: R4 package contains SubstanceAmount definition and references from SubstancePolymer
facts.newValue: R6 package-wide search found no `SubstanceAmount` references

facts.note: This is evidence of remodeling, not a same-identity replacement.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The expected R6 file is absent, the R6 package index has no `SubstanceAmount` StructureDefinition, and text search found no use of the name. `SubstanceDefinition` has amount-related elements, but their paths and content model differ, so they are not a renamed datatype.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct identity and validation break. Any R4 profile, extension, validator, schema, generated class, or parent element that expects the `SubstanceAmount` datatype cannot resolve that datatype in the R6 package. R4 instance fragments nested at elements typed as `SubstanceAmount` do not have a same-type R6 destination; validation must instead occur against a different parent-specific R6 model.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: The datatype appears limited in R4 core usage to draft substance-definition material, especially `SubstancePolymer`, so broad clinical prevalence is likely low. The business and regulatory impact can still be material for medicinal product, substance definition, or chemistry master-data systems.

justification.inferredGoal: Consolidate or remodel the draft R4 substance-definition datatype model into R6 context-specific `SubstanceDefinition` elements.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep `SubstanceAmount` in R6 as a deprecated compatibility datatype while allowing new R6 substance models to use context-specific fields.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal of retiring or remodeling a draft substance amount abstraction is reasonable, but complete removal of the canonical datatype was not the only base-design path. A deprecated carry-forward StructureDefinition would have preserved most R4 `SubstanceAmount` type references and generated-model expectations while still letting R6 prefer `SubstanceDefinition` context-specific amount elements. Without evidence that merely retaining the type would undermine the R6 model, the identity-level break looks probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The strongest less-breaking base R6 design would be to include `StructureDefinition/SubstanceAmount` unchanged or minimally updated, mark it deprecated/legacy, and avoid using it for new R6 substance content. That is different from a conversion tool or extension workaround: it preserves the base canonical type in the R6 package. The tradeoff is carrying a draft abstraction that the substance model may have intentionally outgrown, but this would not force duplicate same-resource amount fields unless R6 also chose to expose both old and new representations in the same parent model.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Retains an obsolete draft type in the base package, but avoids breaking canonical/type references with only moderate long-term cost if new R6 elements do not use it.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `SubstanceAmount` as a complex-type StructureDefinition with type `SubstanceAmount` and base `BackboneElement`.
The R6 package index has no StructureDefinition entry for `SubstanceAmount`.
A package-wide search for `SubstanceAmount` found no matches in the R6 package.
R4 core uses `SubstanceAmount` in three `SubstancePolymer` element paths.

examples.examplesMd: The JSON is an illustrative nested R4 `SubstanceAmount` value, not a complete standalone FHIR resource. In R4 it could appear inside a parent element typed as `SubstanceAmount`; in R6 there is no same datatype definition against which this fragment can be validated.

findings.narrativeMd: `SubstanceAmount` was not merely changed; it is absent from the R6 core package. This affects systems at the canonical identity level: type registries, generated classes, validators, profile differential processing, and transforms that resolve `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/SubstanceAmount` will fail unless they special-case the migration.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4 instance containing a nested `SubstanceAmount` value can be valid against an R4 parent definition, but there is no R6 datatype with the same name or canonical URL. Strict R6 validation therefore cannot accept the fragment as `SubstanceAmount`; it must be transformed into some other R6 structure first. This is primarily an R4-to-R6 break rather than an R6-to-R4 round-trip issue for the same datatype, because R6 has no `SubstanceAmount` datatype to round-trip.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all canonical references and generated classes for `SubstanceAmount`. For each use, map in the context of the parent artifact rather than applying a simple rename. For R4 core usage, analyze `SubstancePolymer` and likely destination modeling in `SubstanceDefinition`; preserve source values in extensions or audit metadata where a lossless mapping is not clear.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible path could have kept the datatype as deprecated or supplied a compatibility profile with a normative ConceptMap. That would have preserved old validators and generated code while allowing new R6 models to prefer context-specific elements. The tradeoff is that R6 would continue carrying a draft R4 datatype abstraction that the ballot model appears to have retired.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm against official ballot narrative or change logs before making irreversible migration decisions; the local package evidence proves absence but not the standards workgroup rationale.

findings.title: R4 SubstanceAmount content model has no lossless one-to-one R6 amount mapping

oldState.summary: R4 reusable datatype contains `amount[x]` (Quantity, Range, string), `amountType`, `amountText`, and `referenceRange.lowLimit/highLimit`.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 packages quantitative value, qualitative text, measurement type, and low/high reference limits in one reusable datatype.

newState.summary: Closest R6 substance amount concepts are split across context-specific `SubstanceDefinition` elements.
newState.narrativeMd: `SubstanceDefinition.moiety.amount[x]` supports Quantity or string with `measurementType`; `SubstanceDefinition.relationship.amount[x]` supports Quantity, Ratio, or string with separate `ratioHighLimitAmount` and `comparator`. These are similar concepts but not the same element identity or shape.

facts.note: R4 `Range` is not a choice type in the closest R6 elements; R6 `Ratio` is not a choice type in R4 `SubstanceAmount.amount[x]`.

facts.oldValue: SubstanceAmount.amountType CodeableConcept with no local binding

facts.newValue: No exact separate field in the closest R6 amount structures; text may need amountString or extension depending on context
No direct low/high Quantity pair in closest R6 amount structures; relationship has ratioHighLimitAmount as Ratio only

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 elements were selected because their definitions describe quantitative substance moiety or relationship amounts and because R6 has no `SubstanceAmount` datatype. The match is conceptual, not canonical.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Once the removed datatype is mapped to R6, data loss or manual decisions are likely for some values. R4 `Range` and `referenceRange.lowLimit/highLimit` do not map cleanly to the closest R6 `Ratio`-oriented high-limit model, while R6 `amountRatio` and `ratioHighLimitAmount` cannot be represented as native R4 `SubstanceAmount.amount[x]` values. This affects conversion, generated mappers, and round-trip tests more than ordinary validation of a same-name element.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Incorrect amount conversion can change the interpretation of active moiety, relationship ratio, or substance quantity information. The affected domain is specialized, but the consequences can matter for medicinal product or regulatory substance data.

justification.inferredGoal: Replace a generic reusable draft amount datatype with amount fields tailored to specific substance-definition contexts.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Add R4-compatible amount choices and low/high/text/type fields to the relevant R6 `SubstanceDefinition` amount contexts, or carry a deprecated `SubstanceAmount`-shaped backbone alongside the new fields.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred R6 goal is to replace a generic draft datatype with amount modeling tailored to moiety and relationship contexts, including R6-specific ratio semantics. That goal is reasonable, and a fully backward-compatible content model would have had material costs: systems could encode the same fact in old and new shapes, validators would need precedence rules, and mappings would still have to decide which R6 context an old generic value belongs in. Because the less-breaking path is incomplete and costly rather than cleanly equivalent, the structural split is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base design could have made the closest R6 amount elements accept the R4 shapes directly, for example by adding `Range` where only `Quantity|string` or `Quantity|Ratio|string` is allowed, preserving separate `amountText`, `amountType`, and `referenceRange.lowLimit/highLimit` equivalents, or allowing a deprecated `SubstanceAmount`-compatible backbone in the relevant R6 contexts. This would preserve many R4 instances better than relying on post-hoc conversion guidance. It would still be only a partial alternative because it cannot infer the correct R6 context for every old use, does not naturally represent new R6 `Ratio`/`ratioHighLimitAmount` semantics back in R4, and would leave two same-resource representations for similar amount facts.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Covers many R4 values, but creates duplicate representations, context-mapping ambiguity, validation complexity, and a risk that legacy amount shapes persist indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 `amount[x]` permits Quantity, Range, or string.
R4 models optional low and high reference limits as Quantity children.
Closest R6 moiety amount element permits Quantity or string and has a separate measurementType.
Closest R6 relationship amount element permits Quantity, Ratio, or string and has separate ratioHighLimitAmount and comparator elements.
R6 uses an example binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/substance-amount-type` on closest amount type/comparator elements.

migrationExampleJson.migrationDecision: Choose a target R6 context and decide whether Range/text are represented as amountString, context-specific Ratio fields, or preserved in extensions.

examples.examplesMd: The R6 example illustrates a native `Ratio` amount and ratio high limit. R4 `SubstanceAmount.amount[x]` has no `Ratio` choice, so a lossless R6-to-R4 transform would need an extension, string encoding, or another profile-specific representation.

findings.narrativeMd: The closest R6 amount fields are not a structural rename of the R4 datatype. They divide amount semantics across moiety and relationship contexts and change available choice types. That means migration code must know the parent context and cannot simply copy `SubstanceAmount.amount[x]`, `amountType`, `amountText`, and `referenceRange` into a single R6 object.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: For R4-to-R6, the removed datatype already forces transformation; this finding explains why the transformation can be lossy or ambiguous. For R6-to-R4, `SubstanceDefinition.relationship.amountRatio` and `ratioHighLimitAmount` have no native R4 `SubstanceAmount` counterpart because R4 permits `Quantity`, `Range`, and `string`, not `Ratio`. Strict generated mappers and round-trip comparison tests should therefore treat this as high representability risk.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Build mappings per parent context. Preserve R4 `Range`, `amountText`, and reference-range limits explicitly when no R6 target is semantically equivalent. For R6-to-R4, decide whether `Ratio` values are out of scope, transformed to strings, or carried in extensions. Test Quantity, Range, string, free-text, low/high reference range, Ratio, and comparator cases separately.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The split may be semantically cleaner because moiety and relationship amounts mean different things, but a compatibility layer could have supplied a lossless transition path. The less-breaking alternative would be explicit cross-version extensions and a ConceptMap documenting each old field's destination and each unsupported R6 field's R4 representation.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Because the match to `SubstanceDefinition` is inferred from local definitions, confirm with official R6 narrative before standardizing a transformation.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: R4 `SubstanceAmount` has no local `Reference`-typed elements, so there are no local reference target changes to assess.

The R4 differential has no local invariants on the business elements. Snapshot constraints such as `ele-1` and `ext-1` are inherited/base-extension constraints and are out of scope for this datatype report.

R4 `SubstanceAmount.amountType` is a `CodeableConcept` with no local binding. R6 closest elements add example bindings to `substance-amount-type`, but because there is no same R6 `SubstanceAmount` element this is treated as migration context rather than a local binding-strength change on the datatype.
No local R4 business element is marked as a modifier. `modifierExtension` behavior is inherited from `BackboneElement` and is out of scope.
The local R4 business elements are unsliced. Extension slicing is inherited infrastructure and not counted as a local `SubstanceAmount` change.
No fixed, pattern, or default values are present on R4 `SubstanceAmount` local elements.
No local R4 maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue constraints were found.
All R4 local business elements are summary elements, but no same R6 datatype exists for flag comparison. This is subsumed by the artifact-removal finding rather than a distinct summary-flag change.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 introduces an example substance-amount-type binding on closest amount-related fields
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is not a direct breaking change to `SubstanceAmount` because the R4 datatype has no local binding and the R6 binding is on different context-specific `SubstanceDefinition` elements with `example` strength.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: When migrating `amountType`-like content, consider aligning local codes with `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/substance-amount-type` where possible, but do not treat the example binding as a required-code validation constraint.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 amount semantics are embedded in substance-definition contexts
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: The presence of R6 context-specific amount fields is not itself a breaking change to the removed datatype; the breaking effect is the absence of the datatype and the ambiguous conversion path captured in the findings.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Use the parent context to decide whether R4 content belongs in a moiety amount, a relationship amount, or another R6 substance-definition structure.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R4 core references `SubstanceAmount` from three `SubstancePolymer` paths, while the R6 package has no `SubstancePolymer` StructureDefinition. The parent resource report should own those resource-level removals or migrations.

`SubstanceDefinition` contains the closest R6 amount-related elements and is the likely destination for at least some substance amount semantics. Its report should assess the resource-level remodel in detail.
R6 uses this value set as an example binding on closest amount type/comparator elements. Terminology review can refine migration guidance for `amountType`-like content.

`SubstanceAmount` derived from `BackboneElement` in R4. Any base infrastructure changes to `id`, `extension`, or `modifierExtension` are intentionally excluded here and should be handled by the base artifact analysis.

analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review official ballot narrative, change proposals, or published cross-version change notes for the substance-definition area.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No computable ConceptMap was available to validate the inferred mapping from R4 `SubstanceAmount` fields to R6 `SubstanceDefinition` fields.
